title: Strict JSON fallback and sampling-compatibility simulation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Build a reproducible simulation harness that evaluates strict JSON enforcement behavior when streaming outputs, tool/function calls, and probabilistic sampling interact. We want to quantify how different sampling parameters, sentinel insertion strategies, and decoder backoff policies affect schema adherence and recovery rates across model families and quantization profiles. Scope: - End-to-end simulation (request -> streaming -> constrained decoder -> fallback) across 6 model variants and 3 hardware profiles. - Injected interleaved tool-call tokens and partial stream truncations to measure graceful degradation. - Produce actionable config knobs (fallback thresholds, sentinel placement heuristics, retry/backoff strategies) and acceptance metrics for runtime default policy. Out of scope: model retraining or fine-tuning; large-scale infra provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation harness can run deterministic scenarios with seedable RNG and produce per-trial schema adherence and latency distributions.
Define and validate at least three fallback policies (lenient-repair, strict-fallback, progressive-relax) and measure their trade-offs on precision/recall of structured fields.
Provide a compatibility matrix mapping model variant + quantization profile + sampling temperature to expected adherence and recommended default policy.
Create a runbook summarizing how runtime should choose fallback policy given latency SLO and customer impact tier.
All test artifacts (configs, sample prompts, golden schemas) are checked into the test harness repo and linked in the ticket.
Telemetry hooks for per-request sentinel counts, repair-rate, and fallback-trigger reasons are defined and validated in the console dashboard.
steps: Design matrix: enumerate models (open-7b, open-13b, rdl-6b-quant, rdl-13b-quant), temps [0.0, 0.3, 0.7], top_p [0.9, 0.95], streaming chunk sizes [8, 32, 128].
Implement a deterministic stream fuzzer that can: insert tool-call delimiters mid-stream, drop random chunks, and corrupt bytes to simulate truncation.

Extend constrained-decoder harness to expose: sentinel injection points, repair heuristics (bracket completion, schema-aware templating), and policy hooks for immediate fallback to safe-model variants.
Run exhaustive grid of scenarios for initial smoke (4 models x 3 temps x 3 chunk sizes x 3 fuzz levels). Collect schema-adherence rate, median latency, 95th latency, and token cost estimate.
Analyze false-repair cases where repair yields semantically incorrect but schema-valid outputs; surface top 10 prompt patterns causing these.
Ship dashboards: per-scenario artifact with heatmaps and recommended default fallback policy per model/profile.
Draft runtime change proposal to wire default policy 'progressive-relax' for hosted API with opt-out for enterprise Dedicated customers; include TTL for canary and rollback criteria.
Create synthetic canary traffic for console and runtime test clusters to validate telemetry and alerting (fallback rate > 4% triggers pager).
risks: Repair heuristics may produce schema-valid but semantically wrong outputs, leading to silent downstream corruption.
Simulation results may not fully extrapolate to production due to traffic diversity and prompt engineering differences.
Increased compute from repair/backoff policies may push token costs above acceptable thresholds for some customers.
Telemetry noise could mask root causes unless we tag experiments with run-id and config fingerprints.
Rollout of stricter enforcement could increase error rates for customers relying on permissive decoding; must offer migration path.
